## Contributing

Contributions from community are key to make NodeGoat a high quality comprehensive resource. Lets make NodeGoat awesome together!

### Ways to Contribute
Depending on your preference, you can contribute in various ways. Here are tasks planned for [upcoming release](https://github.com/OWASP/NodeGoat/milestones).
You can also open an issue, sending a PR, or get in touch on [Gitter Chat](https://gitter.im/OWASP/NodeGoat) or [Slack](https://owasp.slack.com/messages/project-nodegoat/)

If sending PR, once code is ready to commit, run:

npm run precommit

This command uses `js-beautifier` to indent the code and verifies these [coding standards](https://github.com/OWASP/NodeGoat/blob/master/.jshintrc) using `jsHint`. Please resolve all `jsHint` errors before committing the code.
     ```

#### Customizing the Default Application Configuration

By default the application will be hosted on port 4000 and will connect to a MongoDB instance at localhost:27017. To change this set the environment variables `PORT` and `MONGODB_URI`.

Other settings can be changed by updating the [config file](https://github.com/OWASP/NodeGoat/blob/master/config/env/all.js).

### OPTION 2 - Run NodeGoat on Docker

The repo includes the Dockerfile and docker-compose.yml necessary to set up the app and db instance, then connect them together.

1) Install [docker](https://docs.docker.com/installation/) and [docker compose](https://docs.docker.com/compose/install/) 

2) Clone the github repository:
   ```
   git clone https://github.com/OWASP/NodeGoat.git
   ```

3) Go to the directory:
   ```
   cd NodeGoat
   ```

4) Build the images:
   ```
   docker-compose build
   ```

5) Run the app, this starts the NodeGoat application at http://localhost:4000/:
   ```
   docker-compose up
   ```

### OPTION 3 - Deploy to Heroku

This option uses a free ($0/month) Heroku node server.

Though not essential, it is recommended that you fork this repository and deploy the forked repo.
This will allow you to fix vulnerabilities in your own forked version, then deploy and test it on Heroku.

1) Set up a publicly accessible MongoDB instance:
   1) [Deploy a MongoDB Atlas free tier cluster](https://docs.atlas.mongodb.com/tutorial/deploy-free-tier-cluster/) (M0 Sandbox)
   2) [Enable network access](https://docs.atlas.mongodb.com/security/ip-access-list/#add-ip-access-list-entries) to the cluster from anywhere (CIDR range 0.0.0.0/0)
   3) [Add a database user](https://docs.atlas.mongodb.com/tutorial/create-mongodb-user-for-cluster/) to the cluster

2) Deploy NodeGoat to Heroku by clicking the button below:

   [![Deploy](https://www.herokucdn.com/deploy/button.png)](https://heroku.com/deploy)

   In the Create New App dialog, set the `MONGODB_URI` config var to the connection string of your MongoDB Atlas cluster.
   This can be viewed in the cluster's [connect dialog](https://docs.atlas.mongodb.com/tutorial/connect-to-your-cluster/#connect-to-your-atlas-cluster).
   Select "Connect your application", set the driver to "Node.js" and the version to "2.2.12 or later".
   This will give a connection string in the form:
   ```
   mongodb://<username>:<password>@<cluster>/<dbname>?ssl=true&replicaSet=<rsname>&authSource=admin&retryWrites=true&w=majority
   ```
   The `<username>` and `<password>` fields need filling in with the details of the database user added earlier. The `<dbname>` field sets the name of the
   database nodegoat will use in the cluster (eg "nodegoat"). The other fields will already be filled in with the correct details for your cluster.

content.text:
I've fixed the vulnerabilities an attacker could reach over the network: in the web framework (express) and its request handling, in session handling, in the database driver, and in the markdown renderer used on the memos page. The app still works end to end, and the project test suite and linter pass.

**Upgrades** (only the packages that needed to change; others left alone)

| Package | Before → after | What it fixes |
|---|---|---|
| express | 4.16.4 → ^4.22.3 | Redirect XSS and open redirect, plus its sub-packages: query-string prototype pollution and DoS, route-matching ReDoS, IP spoofing, template injection |
| body-parser | 1.18.3 → ^1.20.9 | Denial-of-service bugs in request body parsing |
| express-session | 1.15.6 → ^1.19.0 | Its cookie and response-header sub-packages |
| mongodb | 2.2.36 → ^3.7.4 | Critical deserialization flaw in its BSON library (now bson 1.1.6), and a driver DoS |
| marked | 0.3.5 → 4.3.0 (still pinned) | XSS on the memos page (sanitizer bypass, `javascript:` links) and ReDoS |

**Code changes** (the new versions have breaking API changes, so version bumps alone would have broken the app)
- **`server.js`:** `require("marked")` now returns an object, not a function, so the memos page would have crashed. It now uses `const { marked } = require("marked")`. The mongodb 3 connect callback returns a client, so the app takes the database from `client.db()`.
- **`artifacts/db-reset.js`:** the same mongodb client change, so `npm run db:seed` still works.

**Compatibility rules followed**
- I kept the lockfile in its existing v2 format so older npm versions can still read it.
- The project supports Node 8–14 (CI and the `node:12` Docker image). `marked` 4.x officially requires Node 12+, but I checked that it and the other upgraded packages load and render on Node 10. I didn't test Node 8, which the old Travis config still lists.
- Lint passes with the CI command (`npx jshint .`).

**Testing**
- I ran MongoDB in Docker, seeded the database and drove the app over HTTP: login/logout, failed login, dashboard, profile view and update, contributions, allocations, memos, research, tutorial pages, signup, and the admin benefits page. All 23 checks passed before and after the change.
- I confirmed the memo XSS is closed. The `[x](javascript:alert(1))` input that 0.3.5 let through renders as plain text in 4.3.0, and the ReDoS-style inputs finish in milliseconds.
- `run_tests` passes, but it's only a placeholder "smoke" line, so the journey above is the real check.
- The server log now shows deprecation warnings, from mongodb (`insert`, `update`, `findAndModify`) and from `marked` (the `sanitize` option). They're harmless and everything still works.

**Left unchanged, because they can't be reached from a request**
- **helmet, csurf, dont-sniff-mimetype** (and their `connect`, `debug`, `ms` and `cookie@0.3.1` sub-packages): only appear in commented-out code, so they are never loaded.
- **forever** (the process manager in the `Procfile`) and its sub-packages: they only handle the operator's own command-line options and config, never request data. Fixing them needs a major version upgrade.
- **swig**: there is no fixed version. Its flaw needs attacker-controlled template files, and here templates are fixed files in the repo with user data only filled in as values.
- **underscore**: imported in `config/config.js` but never called, so the affected functions (`_.template`, `_.flatten`, `_.isEqual`) are never used.
- **Dev-only tools** (cypress, nodemon, grunt, selenium, zaproxy and so on): not part of the running app.

NodeGoat is a deliberately vulnerable training app, and I only changed dependencies. Its intentional code-level lessons (autoescape off, the SSRF in research, the commented-out helmet/CSRF fixes) are left as they were. The tutorial page about the `marked` flaw still describes the old version.
